public_rationale: Vectara's hallucination leaderboard, published 19 November 2025, found that notable thinking models still hallucinated in summaries. It reported GPT-5, Claude Sonnet 4.5, GPT-OSS-120B, Grok-4 and DeepSeek-R1 all above 10%, and the just-released Gemini-3-pro at 13.6% (e1, e2). A survey by Song, Han and Goodman, submitted to arXiv on 5 February 2026, says significant reasoning failures persist in LLMs, 'occurring even in seemingly simple scenarios' (e3). That matches the plain reading of 'boneheaded errors.' Nothing in the evidence shows that hallucinations or simple-task errors had been eliminated. Both parts of the claim hold for November 2025 to February 2026.
limitations: Vectara measures faithfulness in summaries only; it does not cover other kinds of hallucination.
The OpenAI system card figures for GPT-5.2 were not read from the primary source.
'Boneheaded' has no threshold; the support rests on the survey's statement about failures in simple scenarios, not on a measured rate.
The survey abstract does not say how often simple-scenario failures occur in frontier models.

our_interpretation: Plain reading: current frontier LLMs around February 2026 still produce false or unsupported content at measurable rates, and still fail at some tasks that are simple for people.
'Boneheaded errors' read as failures on easy or simple problems, not a specific rate.

criteria.contradiction_condition: Evidence that frontier LLMs in this period had effectively eliminated hallucinations and simple-task errors.
